column1: # Generated by scripts/corpus/merge-forms.ts — one row per pair of cards that are forms of
# each other, merged or kept, with the reason. The authority is FORM_RULINGS in
# form-rulings.ts; this file is the readable record of what it did.

column7: why
abhängen von depends on; plain abhängen is the colloquial hang out, and also to unhook something. Three senses, and only one takes von.
eine Prüfung bestehen passes an exam; bestehen aus is what a thing is made of. Unrelated senses that happen to share a lemma.
bitten also takes a person plus a zu-infinitive — «Ich bitte dich, kurz zu warten» — which the um-pattern does not cover. (The A1 example was the um-pattern and is fixed separately.)

die Medien is the press and broadcasting — a B1 word in its own right — while das Medium at C1 is a medium in the technical or spiritualist sense. Same relationship as Schuld/Schulden, and the four-level gap is the evidence.
denken introduces a thought — «Ich denke, dass …» — while denken an is directed at a person or a thing. Both are needed. (The A1 card's example was the governed pattern and is fixed separately.)

column6: keeper relevelled C1→B1; retired sector Fitness and training
column7: Same defect: Schweiss for Schweiß. Here the misspelled card is the *lower* one, so the correct spelling takes B1 — a merge never takes a word away from the learner who had it.
die Alpen is a proper name. die Alp is an alpine pasture (and, separately, a nightmare); the mountain range is not its plural in any useful sense.
das Angeln is angling, the nominalised infinitive of angeln; die Angeln would be fishing rods. Neuter, again.
das Reisen is the nominalised infinitive — travelling, the activity — not the plural of die Reise (a trip). Neuter, as every nominalised infinitive is.

die Schulden (debts) and die Schuld (guilt, fault) have parted company in meaning. German uses the plural for the money sense and the singular for the moral one; teaching them as one card would teach neither.
der Westen is the compass point; die Weste is a waistcoat. Unrelated words that collide only because Weste happens to pluralise to Westen.
Das Buch gehört mir — ownership, bare dative. Der Wolf gehört zu den Raubtieren — membership, with zu. Different constructions and different meanings.
gelten is to be valid; gelten als is to be regarded as. The pattern card also carries a nominative complement, which is rare enough to be worth its own card.
rechnen calculates; rechnen mit expects. A learner who conflates them writes «Ich rechne mit 12» for arithmetic.

regelmässig is the pre-1996 spelling of regelmäßig, which the corpus already cards correctly at A2 — and the B1 card taught the old spelling in its example too («Regelmässiges Training …»). Keeper stays at A2, the lower level.
abstimmen votes; sich abstimmen coordinates with somebody. Unrelated in use.
etwas anpassen adjusts a thing; sich anpassen adapts yourself to a place or a rule. The second is the word the integration texts use.
etwas auflösen dissolves or winds something up; sich auflösen is the thing dissolving by itself. Same transitive/inchoative pair.
aufregen upsets somebody; sich aufregen is getting upset. Transitive against inchoative, the commonest German reflexive pattern.
jemanden beschäftigen employs or keeps somebody busy; sich beschäftigen mit occupies yourself with a subject.
einsetzen deploys or inserts something; sich einsetzen für campaigns for a cause. The reflexive has a fixed preposition the plain verb does not take.
einsetzen deploys or inserts; sich einsetzen für campaigns for a cause.
etwas entscheiden settles a question; sich entscheiden is making up your own mind. A learner needs both and confuses them constantly.
entspannen relaxes something — Muskeln, eine Lage — and is also used intransitively; sich entspannen is a person relaxing. Kept, though the two glosses could separate better.
erinnern reminds somebody of something; sich erinnern an remembers. Different subjects and different objects — the pair that made this whole shape visible.
sich orientieren finds your bearings; sich orientieren an takes its lead from something — «Der Preis orientiert sich an der Qualität». The preposition changes the meaning, not just the frame.

Both are current and both are needed: man streitet **über** eine Frage, but man streitet **sich mit** jemandem. The two glosses currently say the same thing, which is a gloss defect on the pair and not a reason to delete one of them.
jemanden treffen meets somebody, by arrangement or by chance; sich treffen is two people meeting up. Also treffen = to hit a target, which the reflexive never means.
unterhalten maintains or supports; sich unterhalten holds a conversation. Same level, and still two words.
ein Gesetz verabschieden passes a law — a C1 word from parliamentary German; sich verabschieden says goodbye. The four-level gap is the evidence.
verletzen injures somebody else, and figuratively breaks a rule or a feeling; sich verletzen is injuring yourself.
verstehen understands; sich verstehen gets along with somebody. Only the pronoun separates «Ich verstehe dich» from «Wir verstehen uns».
etwas vorbereiten prepares a thing; sich vorbereiten auf prepares yourself for an exam. Both are ordinary and the plain card's example is genuinely transitive.
etwas vorbereiten prepares a thing; sich vorbereiten auf prepares yourself for an event. Transitive against reflexive-plus-preposition.
vorstellen introduces somebody else; sich vorstellen introduces yourself, and also means to imagine. Three senses, and the pronoun is what selects between them.
stammen aus is an origin in place or time; stammen von is descent from a person or a source, which is the B1 card's sense. Two prepositions, two meanings.
umgehen mit handles or deals with something; plain umgehen avoids or bypasses it — and the two even stress differently. Merging them would be the umfahren mistake this file already warns about.
verfügen über has something at your disposal; plain verfügen decrees. (The B2 card's example is the über-pattern and is fixed separately.)

voc:A2:sich erinnern was itself retired later the same day, into voc:A2:sich erinnern an + A — one card twice at one level, which the governed shape found. The keep still holds and is restated against the surviving card in the governed block below; this row is the record of it being asked first.

Both cards were folded into voc:A1:der/die Bekannte by the adjectival-noun dedupe. The gendered pair was worth keeping against *one* neutral card that did not exist yet; once the der/die card was the canonical one, three cards for one word was not a distinction, it was three schedules.
warten alone is intransitive — «Warte kurz!» — and warten auf takes an accusative object. The pattern is the B1 fact; the bare verb is A1. (The A1 example was the pattern and is fixed separately.)
ziehen pulls; ziehen nach moves house. The second is idiomatic and unguessable from the first.
